title: NBI — Bank Account Stories | Women
summary: A documentary-style campaign series for the National Bank of Iraq, exploring financial aspirations through the personal experiences of Iraqi women. Comprising three individual stories and a teaser, the campaign approaches banking through everyday ambitions, personal decisions, and the desire for a more secure future.

meta.title: NBI — Bank Account Stories | Women | Rafat Mhalla
meta.description: A three-film NBI documentary series. Each film gives one Iraqi woman space to tell how she opened her account with NBI and what changed for her. Creative direction by Rafat Mhalla and Mohammad Jalal at Vision House.

blocks.title: NBI Bank Account Stories | Women — teaser

blocks.body:
A story centred on the aspiration of owning a home and creating a personal space for the future.

The film connects this ambition with the possibilities of home financing, focusing on the emotional significance of reaching a long-held goal.

blocks.title: The Key to Your Dream Home | NBI Housing Loan

blocks.body:
A story about planning for the next generation.

The narrative explores the decisions a mother makes while thinking about her children's security, opportunities, and future.

blocks.title: Building Your Child's Future with NBI

blocks.body: A story about independence, ambition, and the desire to move forward without allowing financial limitations to define personal progress.

blocks.title: Don't Wait for Salary Day | Real Success Stories

blocks.body:
The creative approach places each woman's experience at the centre of the narrative.

Rather than relying on conventional advertising language, the films are structured around personal stories and relatable financial goals.

Each film explores a different perspective, allowing the campaign to connect banking services with moments that carry genuine personal meaning.

The visual direction is intimate, restrained, and human.

Carefully considered framing, natural performances, and subtle lighting transitions support the emotional development of each story.

The creative approach allows the individual voices and experiences to remain central to the films.

The planned approach favours locked-off framing, close and medium shots, soft natural light, and gentle shadows in the past that warm in the present. Silence or light ambience opens each story, with piano or strings as the story turns, keeping the voice clear and central.
